diagnosis.narrative: The series is dominated by a strong downward trend (a net fall of ~249% of its level). There is little seasonal structure. The series is quite predictable: its energy concentrates in a few structured frequencies. The series reads as non-stationary by the ADF/KPSS tests. A few outliers stand out (2 points, ~0% of the sample). Across validation windows the model ranking is unstable (Kendall tau 0.041), which favours a robust combination.

We need a new combination not tested. Options: A trimmed_mean pool_full, B best_single pool1 rf, C dba pool2, D best_single pool2 rf, E dba pool3, F best_single pool3 rf, G mean pool4, H median pool4.

We haven't tested any with pool4. So choose maybe mean pool4. That seems plausible.

attempts.rationale: deterministic baseline: plain mean of the full pool
deterministic baseline: median, robust to outlying models
deterministic baseline: DTW barycenter of the full pool
deterministic baseline: mean over the 5 models with the most consistent ranking across windows
deterministic baseline: trimmed_mean over the 5 models with the most consistent ranking across windows
deterministic baseline: mean over the 7 models with the most consistent ranking across windows
deterministic baseline: trimmed_mean over the 7 models with the most consistent ranking across windows
deterministic baseline: mean over the 9 models with the most consistent ranking across windows
deterministic baseline: trimmed_mean over the 9 models with the most consistent ranking across windows
deterministic baseline: weights from a gradient-boosted model trained across every other series in this run (leave-one-series-out)
Test a trimmed‑mean over the full pool to see if trimming improves robustness beyond the mean baseline.
Test a best_single strategy with the full pool using the rf model to see if a single strong performer beats the mean baseline.
Test a robust median combination over the highly consistent pool1 to see if it beats the best_single rf.
Test a robust median combination over pool1 to see if it can beat the best_single rf.
Test a weighted combination with inverse-error weighting on the small, stable pool1 to see if it beats the current best single rf.
Test a weighted combination on pool2 using inverse_error weights to see if a more focused pool improves over the best_single rf.
Test a robust median combination over pool2 to see if it can beat best_single rf.
Test a weighted combination using inverse_error weights on pool3 to see if a different pool improves over the best single rf.
Test a robust median over pool2 to see if it beats the current best_single rf while staying simple.
Try a deterministic weighted average via DBA on pool1 to see if it improves over plain mean/median on that small pool.
Test a robust median combination over pool3 to see if it beats the current best_single rf.
Try a simple mean over pool4 to see if expanding the pool improves performance.

decision.justification: Selected 'best_single rf' (an agent proposal) as the best of 22 backtested attempts, score 0.65. Series context: trend strength 0.8651 and seasonal strength 0.1038; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.041); 1 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.504.
